key_insight: Tokens do not all need the same number of experts: easy tokens can be routed more cheaply, while uncertain tokens deserve more expert capacity. CARE uses the router's own confidence as a signal to adapt how many experts each token receives.
problem_solved: Standard Mixture-of-Experts LoRA routes every token to a fixed top-k experts, which wastes compute on confident tokens and can underserve ambiguous ones. This paper addresses the mismatch between token difficulty and fixed routing capacity.
method: Use the router's output distribution as a per-token uncertainty estimate: peaked distributions indicate high confidence, flatter ones indicate uncertainty.
Admit experts adaptively based on confidence rather than using a fixed k for all tokens.
Allocate more experts to uncertain tokens and fewer experts to easy tokens to better balance accuracy and efficiency.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, CARE offers a way to make LoRA-based expert routing more compute-efficient without treating every token the same. It can improve resource allocation in adaptation-heavy models by focusing capacity where it is most needed.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of fixed top-k routing vs confidence-adaptive routing

paper_title: Spend Experts Where You Are Unsure: Confidence-Adaptive Routing for Mixture-of-Experts LoRA
paper_authors: Tom Saliencro, Rohan Desai, Priya Nair, Maya Lindqvist, Daniel Whitmore
